Item One: We know they are lying.

Recently, Allen St. Pierre, NORML's Executive Director told me about an interesting experience he had in a non-debate with a representative of the Drug Czar's office.
See
 "Thank you Miss Rosa" By Allen St. Pierre. One Brave Person Can Make The Crucial Difference.

I call it a non-debate because no one from the DEAland federal government will debate anyone from NORML, so Allen was speaking to a group of approximately 100 first year law students at American University in Washington, shortly after one of the Czar's little helpers had spoken to them.

Allen began by asking the students what the main points were in the government's official presentation. Predictably, they were..

 Ho hum. What else is new?

Then Allen asked them to raise their hands if they thought that they had been lied to. Almost every hand in the room went up, and, remember, this was before Allen had spoken!

In other words, a group of first year law students from the DARE generation, who had been subjected to a massive prohibitionist propaganda campaign all of their lives, recognized that a major government program was based on deliberate lies.
From 2000, See
 Counterproductivity of DARE Programs Shown In Studies And Demonstrated In Great Anti-Prohibitionist Editorial In Michigan Daily. 2 Articles and an Editorial

If the real purpose of prohibitionist propaganda was to impact cannabis use by students, the Drug Czar's office should be very worried, but their real targets are the police, to maintain their morale, the politicians, to maintain their power, and the media, to keep the general public quiescent.
See
 Reuters Madness and the Subordination of Journalism to Prohibitionist Propaganda. Conning CNN. Lies Lead to Wars, But Then, That Is Their Purpose.

All three of these groups should be very worried; however, the media are the most puzzling piece in the prohibitionist puzzle. Unlike the police and the politicians, the media have no direct stake in the continuation of cannabis prohibition. On the other hand, they have the most direct stake in maintaining their credibility, and if these first year law students know that the government is lying, they also know that the media are lying.
See
 Lies Have Consequences: Police Targeted Anti-Prohibitionist Reporter Because They Believed Lies Told By Their Superiors Who Are Shocked, Of Course.
and

Item Two: Denver Votes To Abolish Pot Penalties

The people of Denver voted this week to decriminalize adult possession of one ounce of marijuana, despite opposition from virtually all of the city's establishment. Oddly, the Denver Post had editorialized against it, even though it has separately endorsed legalization. Prior to a major change in its editorial policy it had even opposed the state's medical cannabis initiative, and was ignored by the voters then as now.
See
 The Denver Post Editorial Page Lies to Its Readers About Medical Marijuana Again

Perhaps the most amusing aspect of this vote was the reaction of the politicians. They really resent it when the voters get uppity and think that democracy means something. That may be alright for the Iraqis, but not in America!

As usual, Jay Leno had the best line: Fifty-three percent of the people approve of having marijuana in Denver, how about that? How does that make Bush feel? He's 14 percent behind pot now.
See
 The Crisis in Democracy, Prohibitionism And The Police Fiasco. Why Will It Work In Iraq, If It Does Not Work In DEAland?
and
 Its The Stupidity, Stupid. How the Prohibitionist Ideology Has Wrecked The Republican Party and Undermined Democracy Everywhere. When Ideology Trumps Reality, The Result is Stupidity.

Item Three: Gallup: Public Support Grows For Legalizing Pot

Although the Denver initiative only called for the complete decriminalization of possession of an ounce, many news stories ran under headlines saying that Denver had voted to legalize marijuana which usually means legalized sales to adults, not just possession.

The fact is that the L-word legalization, not Lesbianism tends to draw more negative responses than regulate and tax. Consequently,when one considers that more than one third of the American people favor legalization after being bombarded with the same prohibitionist propaganda that failed to convince the AU law students, it is a great triumph of individual thinking.
See
 Democracy, Cannabis and the Drug Czar. Arrests Remain Close to Record Levels. Support for Medical Cannabis Now Up to 80%. And 34% Favor Full Legalization. We Are Winning, But The People Are Suffering.

Item Three: The old media are trying to buy their way into the world of the Internet, but they clearly don't understand this world.

Excerpted from the October 27th Guardian: WPP group chief executive Sir Martin Sorrell has accused traditional media owners such as Rupert Murdoch of panic-buying internet companies because of falling ad revenues.

Sir Martin, the country's most influential advertising man and in charge of the world's second largest ad group, said there was "deep cause for concern" among TV and newspaper owners.

"In the last two or three months he has decided to spend or try to spend I think it is about $5bn on internet properties of various sorts," said Sir Martin

"Why is it that he is so preoccupied with this and willing it appears to make investments almost willy-nilly? I think I can use the word panic - that is probably overdoing it but maybe I am not"

Sir Martin said the scale and speed of the digital revolution was "faster and bigger than we could have anticipated".

He said newspapers had succeeded in putting their content onto the internet, but had only just woken up to the fact that they also had to charge for it. He used the example of the New York Times, where he said earnings were down 50%...

Speaking of the New York Times, how did it report the Denver initiative? Very carefully. In an article titled Colorado Cap on Spending Is Suspended there was this sentence: Here in Denver, however, voters approved an ordinance that makes possession of small amounts of marijuana legal. State criminal possession laws still apply, so the Denver measure is considered largely symbolic.

It is not clear whether that appeared in the Times print edition, or if it was just online. On the other hand, The Washington Post did carry a full article about the Denver initiative, but only online, not in its print edition.

Neither paper reported on the latest Gallup poll results, anywhere.

As it happens, the New York Times is deeply embroiled in a scandal over its reporting on the Bush Administration's propaganda leading up to the Iraq war. The publisher has even apologized for being too uncritical in its reporting.
See
 Front Page Fantasy: The New York Times Pushes Fact Free Journalism Supposedly About BC Bud

The Washington Post editorial page is in full cry after the Libby indictments about lying to justify a war, and of course they are outraged by the abuse suffered by suspected terrorists.

On the other hand, they never noticed that a disabled American veteran was being tortured in an American jail, and they contribute more than their fair share to prohibitionist propaganda.
See
 Steve Tuck Now Free and Getting Proper Medical Care. Will Return to Humboldt to Confront Medical Marijuana Cultivation Charges. The Many Issues In a Complex Case.
and

and

The fact is that Rupert Murdoch and the masters of the old media are wasting their money if they think that they can run the Internet the way they ran the old media. The people not just law students know that they have been lied to for decades and they don't have to take it any more. There are only one or two newspapers in most cities, and only a few television stations, but anyone who wants to go beyond the local gatekeepers can do so. The editors and producers are no longer all-powerful.

Item Four: They're rioting in Paris.

As you may have heard, the mostly Moslem and African slums that ring Paris have been torn by rioting for the last week. A variety of causes have been suggested, including an unemployment rate of over 20% for the disaffected youth.

However, an article in today's Los Angeles Times suggests another reason, the drugwar. France is one of the most prohibitionist countries in Western Europe, and enforcement is much more aggressive when racial minorities are involved.
See
 Prohibition and The Prison State. Protecting Youth and Minorities. In DEAland, The UK and France Prisons Are Full.

As a result, the police are even more distrusted than they would be otherwise and organized crime has every reason to foment violence against the police.

Excerpted from The Los Angeles Times

"Violent disturbances are nothing new in the bleak public housing projects on the urban periphery, where intelligence officials say that the two most powerful social forces are the drug underworld and Islamic activism

But the current rioting has lasted longer than in the past and spread alarmingly, authorities say, because of accumulated frustration and tension and incitement by small-time gangsters trying to reassert control over turf. Although Islamic extremism is seen as a serious problem in some of the affected neighborhoods, there is no indication that fundamentalist leaders have encouraged the unrest, officials say.

This week's events have been "extraordinary," said a police intelligence chief who oversees a number of hot spots. "The global situation has been extremely difficult in the slums, even if a lot of people didn't realize that. There has been a convergence of unfortunate events. And now you have the kingpins who are pushing kids to go out and destroy. The kingpins know we need calm to fight the underworld economy.".

"What's in play behind this violence is turf," Julien Dray said during a televised discussion Thursday. "A certain number of religious extremists will say, 'Let us handle things and you will have calm.' Or a certain number of gangsters will say, 'Don't mess with our business and there will be no fires.'

Of course, the prohibitionist regime of Jacque Chirac can never recognize these facts, just as the Bush Administration cannot recognize the damage being done by the drugwar in American cities and even more in our Southern neighbors.
See

Item Five: The menace of the therapeutic state. Coercive rehabilitation

If the police are culturally isolated, the same may be even more of a problem with the quackocracy. The old media hide behind these authority figures but the public has consistently ignored these charlatans who have consistently opposed medical cannabis.

Consider this excerpt from The Australian about a recent prohibitionist conference in Australia:

Acting magistrate Craig Thompson called on governments to wind back the decriminalisation of marijuana and impose "coercive rehabilitation" based on abstinence for people addicted to drugs.

He said it was "totally incomprehensible" that the laws had evolved so people could be fined for smoking a cigarette but cautioned for marijuana use.

"So many are coming before me suffering drug-induced psychosis where marijuana and crystal methamphetamines are the main causes," Mr Thompson told the Adelaide conference.
